_comment: The TypeScript subjects — the TEAM's agreed split, not this harness's invention.
`prior_internal_use: true` means the project already appears in the axiom engine's OWN
TypeScript evaluation corpus (test/typescript/corpus/corpus.tsv in that repo). Those are kept
in the registry because the team's split names them, and they are flagged because a project a
tool was developed against cannot also be neutral ground for measuring it. A number from one is
reported with the flag beside it, exactly as the Java `torture` subject is.
Four of the team's dev projects (immer, remeda, zustand, zod) and five of its held-out projects
(typeorm, axios, nest, trpc, rxjs) carry that flag. The eight dev and five held-out projects
that do not are the ones this benchmark can speak about without qualification, and they are the
A GitHub subject is fetched as a source tarball pinned by COMMIT and SHA-256. There is no
published-artefact equivalent of the Java jar here: TypeScript ships .js and .d.ts, and the
tools under test read .ts, so the repository at a fixed commit is the only reproducible form.

subjects.name: torture
subjects.description: Five families: declared heritage, structural typing, function values, overloads/generics, cross-module name collision.

subjects.name: typedoc
subjects.description: Documentation generator. Large, pure TypeScript, heavy class hierarchies and visitor dispatch. Entered at src/lib: its root tsconfig also governs src/test, and gate 4 refuses a run where the tools would index files the checker's program does not contain.

subjects.name: ts-morph
subjects.description: WAS BLOCKED at gate 0 (48.2%, 17,597/36,501) under its own tsconfig, which includes src/tests (17,086 of its 36,501 call expressions) and reaches @ts-morph/common only through a workspace symlink. With the registry overrides — exclude src/tests, and a `paths` mapping to the declaration file the repository commits at packages/common/lib/ts-morph-common.d.ts — the checker resolves 95.1% (8,364/8,799; issue #28). A wrapper over the TypeScript compiler API; very large generated+handwritten class surface. Sixth TypeScript subject, reported in docs/RESULTS.md, outside the five-subject comparison.

subjects.name: kysely
subjects.description: SQL query builder. Generics-dense, fluent interfaces, many small classes. Entered at src/: its root tsconfig governs that subtree, and the repo also carries an example app and tests the config excludes (gate 4 caught the mismatch).

subjects.name: cheerio
subjects.description: WAS BLOCKED at gate 0 (41.2%; 54.7% with the specs excluded) with a wrong diagnosis: its tsconfig sets `lib: ["ES2015.Core"]`, which REPLACES the default library with one augmentation file, so under the benchmark's staging (no node_modules, hence no @types/node pulling a full lib in) the checker had no declaration for Array, Object, String, Map or Promise at all — 168 of the 251 residual calls were unbound standard-library globals, not the domhandler/domutils/parse5 types the earlier note blamed (issue #55). With the registry overrides — exclude the colocated vitest specs and fixtures, `lib: ["ES2022","DOM"]` — the checker resolves 81.6% (452/554), install-free, the same mechanism ts-morph uses. jQuery-like DOM traversal; medium, idiomatic TS. Reported in docs/RESULTS.md, outside the five-subject comparison.

subjects.name: got
subjects.description: BLOCKED at gate 0. 53.8% over source/ (393/731) under its own tsconfig with the missing `@sindresorhus/tsconfig` base inlined; 162 of the 338 unresolved calls are `is.<x>(...)` into `@sindresorhus/is`, a package that is not on disk and that no tsconfig key can recover. Adding `lib: ["es2022","dom"]` moves the raw figure to 57.9% — above the floor — but adds 0 calls that resolve INTO the subject: the floor would be cleared by resolving library calls that are never scored (#67, comment), so the block stands on the in-subject share, which the report now prints beside the floor for every subject. HTTP client; medium.

subjects.name: type-graphql
subjects.description: Kept, but out of the five-subject comparison at the user's request — replaced by excalidraw. Decorator-driven; 227 uniquely-linked groups. Results remain under typescript/results/.

subjects.name: immer
subjects.description: IN THE ENGINE'S OWN TS CORPUS — a number from this project measures agreement with a project the tool was developed against.

subjects.name: remeda
subjects.description: BLOCKED: checker coverage 35.1% (floor 55%) — the package tsconfig sweeps in `.test-d.ts` type-test files whose call expressions the checker cannot resolve without the vitest types. Also in the engine's own corpus.

subjects.name: excalidraw
subjects.description: WAS HELD OUT; moved to dev on 2026-09-12 at the user's request to replace type-graphql in the five-subject comparison. It is no longer blind. Large React/TypeScript app, 185 .ts + 259 .tsx, JSX component calls throughout — a real stress on tools that emit no call site for a JSX element. MONOREPO PACKAGE: the tools index from packages/ so that the sibling packages the checker types through (@excalidraw/common, element, math, utils) are in their view; the scorer strips the excalidraw/ prefix (issue #20).
